gloss: mental composure; peace of mind; emotional leeway

definitions.gloss: mental composure; peace of mind; emotional leeway
definitions.explanation: The state of having enough emotional or mental space to remain calm, considerate, and unhurried. The psychological capacity to handle situations without stress or panic.

examples.japanese: {心|こころ}の{余裕|よゆう}がない。
examples.english: I have no peace of mind.

examples.japanese: {心|こころ}の{余裕|よゆう}を{持|も}つことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to maintain mental composure.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しすぎて{心|こころ}の{余裕|よゆう}がなくなっていた{自分|じぶん}に{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: I realized I had been too busy and had lost my peace of mind.

notes:
Composed of {心|こころ} (heart, mind) + の (possessive) + {余裕|よゆう} (room, margin, composure). A very common expression in modern Japanese, frequently used in self-help, work-life balance, and wellness contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {心|こころ}の{余裕|よゆう}がある: to have mental composure
- {心|こころ}の{余裕|よゆう}がない: to lack mental composure
- {心|こころ}の{余裕|よゆう}を{持|も}つ: to maintain peace of mind
- {心|こころ}の{余裕|よゆう}を{失|うしな}う: to lose one's composure
- {心|こころ}の{余裕|よゆう}を{取|と}り{戻|もど}す: to regain peace of mind

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気持|きも}ちの{余裕|よゆう}: emotional leeway — very similar, slightly more casual
- {精神的|せいしんてき}{余裕|よゆう}: psychological composure — more formal/clinical
- ゆとり: room, margin — can also refer to mental/temporal slack

USAGE:
Often discussed in the context of {働|はたら}き{方改革|かたかいかく} (work-style reform) and mental health awareness in Japan.
